name: a worn footpath of packed earth between shacks, lighter than the surrounding dirt, with faint wheel ruts and footprints, its edges feathering softly into the dirt with no outline, laid as a path network with crossings and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/track

surfaces.part: packed-earth ground texture, full tile with lighter path network and dirt around it

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256px-wide ground texture tile (every row is 256 wide, no transparent rows or silhouette). It is dirt with lighter path areas, ruts and speckles. It has no standing body, no front face, no edge line, no eave shadow, and no ellipse or roof. The column scan shows only repeating texture bands in similar browns, not a structure. It is flat terrain seen from above, so it has no front face and reads as a top-down surface, which is correct for terrain. The kind matches.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 3 visible tones per tile (dark, mid and light brown), equal to the grass reference's 3 and below the paving reference's 7. Its raw count of 7 colours is low, but the dither-like speckle and clumps keep near-flat coverage at 3%, so there are no big flat fills. Outline is none, which suits a path with feathered edges, and the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral). The path itself is hard to read: the lighter packed-earth strip is barely distinguishable from the surrounding dirt, with only faint lighter patches at the right and some seams between tiles. The wheel ruts and footprints are not clearly visible, and the crossings and dead ends do not come through. The ramp is shallow compared with the Beodeul 5-6 steps per material, and the texture reads as a uniform noise repeat. Overall it is a pleasant but thin ground tile that sits below the references in shading depth, and with the path structure also unclear it would look flatter than the reference next to it.

surfaces.part: packed earth ground tile with ruts and footprints

answer.evidence: The candidate is a seamless, fully opaque 256x192 ground texture, with every row 256 px wide. There is no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical face. The column scan shows only repeating mottled dirt bands and the lighter path areas, with no structural edge. It is a flat top-down terrain tile, which suits the terrain kind, so it has no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours in total and 3 per tile, so the dirt ramp has about 3 steps (light speckle, mid, dark blotch) against roughly 5-6 in the Beodeul pieces. Its 3 visible tones per tile match the grass reference, but the grass gets its richness from 26 raw shades of clumped tufts and a darker patch. The paving reference reaches 7 visible tones. Flat coverage is low at 3%, so there are no true flat fills. The texture is a repetitive dither-and-blotch pattern that looks tiled, with faint seams at tile boundaries. The lighter path band is barely distinguishable from the surrounding dirt, and no ruts, footprints, crossings or dead ends can be read. The soft feathered edge with no outline is correct, and the 0% neutral edge share fits having no outline. Overall it is shallower and flatter than the references, with too little tonal separation, so a careful artist would not place it next to them without it looking thinner. When in doubt, fail.
